rationale:
Top-heavy caricature taken hard: the head is 18px tall on a 59px figure (3.3 heads), the two fists are 12px and 10px wide — each nearly as wide as the torso — and the injector is a 9x15 slab of hardware. Legs are 7 rows of stubby shin, boots 4 rows and no wider than the leg, so all visual mass sits in the top third. This pass changed none of that: the silhouette, pose, proportions, ink skeleton and front-facing cue are pixel-identical to the previous version. What changed is the rendering.

Palette: 24 colours to 55. The old grid ran two values per material with a third only on focal surfaces, which made every panel read as a flat field bounded by ink. Every material now carries a full ramp — coat 8 values, rust 7, helmet 7, skin 5, metal 5, teal 5, bone 4, boot 4, pants 4, hair 3, ink 3 — so forms turn inside their own outline instead of relying on the contour to describe them.

Hue moves with value, it does not just get darker. Each ramp is cool-plum or cool-blue at the bottom and warm at the top: the shell runs #181320 violet to #c6bbb8 warm grey; rust runs #33191f plum through #a6533f to #e2a175; the coat runs #1a2226 blue-green through #46524f to #87907f yellow-green; skin runs #56332f to #e8b18b. The two coolest additions, coat #1a2226 and sky-bounce #2b373c, are gated to the deepest folds of the skirt and the inner leg so the shadow side reads as ambient fill rather than black.

Light stays upper-left and the camera stays 2:1 dimetric, so horizontal faces get the key: the helmet crown, the shoulder band, the brim lip, the fist top planes, the belt and the boot tops each carry the top step of their ramp, then fall diagonally to the lower right. The brightest step of every ramp is reserved for real edge light — a corner where the form meets transparency or an ink seam — which is why #c6bbb8, #e2a175, #f4ece0 and #c0bab8 total under 20 pixels between them. Interior ink is no longer a single value: seams that separate two panels lift to #1e1622 when they part cool materials and #2f1d1c when they part warm ones, so a sleeve seam reads as a seam and not as another outline. #120b10 is still the deepest colour in the legend and still owns the entire outer contour and the two structural cast-shadow rows under the brim and the chin.

Wear is placed, not sprayed: rust dust #6d5342 breaks the helmet hazard band and the mitt knuckles, a scrape of #5b4a3e runs across the shell's right plane and the brim, mud #4a4033 pools on the coat skirt and the left hip, and scuffed leather #503f33 shows on the boot toes and the belt. Grime is clumped by low-frequency noise so it reads as staining rather than static, and it is weighted toward the ground.

Identity budget is unchanged. Rust livery still runs ~25% of the pixels (helmet band, both gauntlets, forearm band, knee wraps, chest patch). Bone-white is still spent almost entirely on the chest cross. Teal is still the ~5% emission budget on goggles, filter port and injector vial — but each of those now has its own specular-to-black ramp instead of three flat values, which is what makes the glass read as glass. No magenta, no chartreuse.

Sacrifices are the same ones as before: a 4-row bare neck that is anatomically long, a planted near-symmetric pose, both hands below the shoulder line. The palette pass buys back a little of the lost drama through value rather than shape — the fists now have hot top planes and near-black undersides, so they read as heavy rather than as flat orange blocks.

Transparency is real: space is alpha 0, the sprite has a true 8-bit alpha channel, alpha is strictly binary (no partial pixels), and no opaque pixel shares an RGB value with the transparent fill, so colour-keying cannot punch holes through it.
frontFacingCue:
Four stacked, unambiguous front cues on a single face plane, each in a value that separates from what is behind it. Unchanged in geometry from the previous version; each is now modelled rather than flat.

(1) A twin-lens goggle band at rows 10-12. Each lens carries its own ramp from a #d6f7ef specular in its upper-left corner down through #8fd9cf and #2f7d78 to #0a1d24 at its lower-right — the brightest marks on the sprite, sitting exactly where eyes belong, framed in ink and set against #241a24 hair and the #4c4753 shell. Two lenses lit identically from the upper-left only reads as a pair of eyes when both are aimed at the camera.

(2) A lit skin face plane at rows 13-19. The goggle band casts a solid #56332f shadow across the top of the cheeks at row 13, the left cheek then steps up through #a86a4f to #cf9067, and a #e8b18b ridge runs down the nose with its shadow immediately to the right. Value separation from the surrounding hair is ~40 at the cheekbone.

(3) A dark respirator mass, #33333a, cupping nose and mouth, with a lit #6f6f77 lip along its top-left edge and a teal filter port pushed off-centre to the viewer's right whose core is #d6f7ef. Mask geometry only makes sense head-on, and the lit top lip proves the mask stands proud of the face.

(4) A lit jaw and chin below it, narrowing over four rows to an 8px chin with a #e8b18b leading edge, so the head silhouette tapers downward the way a face does, not the way a hood or a back-of-skull does.

Supporting it: the helmet brim projects 1px wider than the skull and casts a solid #120b10 row across the brow, which only happens on a peak pointed at the camera; the brim's own front lip is the lightest metal on the head (#c0bab8 at its left corner), which reads as a horizontal surface seen from above.

Head clearance: chin ends at row 19, a full-width ink row at 20, then a 6px bare neck for rows 21-24 against transparent background — modelled as a cylinder with a lit #cf9067 strip on its left and a #56332f core shadow, so it reads as round and recessed. The collar at row 25 opens a 4px ink socket exactly under the neck column and is deliberately kept in the coat's darker steps so the socket survives downscaling. Silhouette goes wide (28px) -> pinch (6px) -> wide (28px). Nothing rises above the shoulder line — no pack, no raised weapon, no antenna.
smallCheck:
Verified by box-filter downscale to 21x28 (head lands at ~8px) and inspected at 8x, plus a 12x16 stress test at 10x. It survives at 28px, with honest losses; 16px is below the design target.

Holds: the head is unmistakably a head facing forward — the goggle band collapses into one bright teal horizontal smear across the upper skull, which is the single most legible mark on the sprite and reads as "eyes, front". The rust hazard band on the helmet now survives downscaling as a distinct orange line because its left end is #e2a175 rather than the same mid rust as everything else, which gives the helmet a two-band structure at 28px it did not have before. The helmet brim keeps the head wider than the neck, the chest cross survives as a pale dab, the two rust fists read as orange blobs at different heights (asymmetry survives), and the injector's teal vial stays visible as a separate held object. The 4px leg gap keeps the legs as two, not one block.

The extra values pay for themselves at small size in one specific way: the coat no longer averages to a single flat grey-green. The shoulder top plane, the mid torso and the skirt land on three separable greys after the box filter, so the figure keeps a light-to-dark diagonal instead of becoming one silhouette-shaped blob. The boots gained a #3d3438 top lip for the same reason — it stops the legs and boots from fusing into one dark rectangle.

Loses: the neck still disappears — head and shoulders merge into one mass at 28px. Separation depends on the value break at the collar (the ink socket blurs into a dark line) and on the brim being wider than the top of the shoulders. The nose ridge, the knee wraps, the finger grooves, the belt buckle, the chest strap and all of the grime vanish into texture — the grime does not turn to noise, it just averages back into its parent material, which is the correct failure mode. The respirator survives only as a dark bar.

Verdict: readable and correctly-oriented at 28px. It reads as "helmeted figure with teal visor, orange band, red cross, orange gloves, held device" — the medic silhouette, not the character. At 48px and up the modelling is fully intact and the figure reads as lived-in hardware rather than flat colour fields.
